All 49 ENA samples are Raoultella sp.1 and sp.2 (EBI title lists '69 Raoultella isolates'; ENA count is 49, paper reports 47 sequenced genomes — minor discrepancy, ~96% coverage). Raoultella is deposited/classified under Klebsiella genus in ENA, explaining the taxon-sample count. Focal strains were deliberately evolved for 5 months in laboratory aquatic microcosms at pH 5.5 to study adaptation in complex communities; ancestral and evolved pooled-colony populations were whole-genome sequenced. This is explicit experimental evolution by novel-environment serial passage, not observational sampling. amr_study graded 'surveillance' because no AMR phenotype or genotype was used as a selection criterion; strains were chosen for their diverse ecological and intrinsic properties. isolation_source and host are proposed as 'water-filled tree hole' reflecting the original environmental source of the ancestral isolates; evolved populations were technically recovered from lab microcosms, but lab culture is not a valid isolation_source per rubric. EBI title discrepancy (69 vs 49 ENA) likely reflects samples attempted but not deposited or a difference in counting replicates vs unique isolates. Collection date midpoint of August 2013–April 2014 span (~9 months) is December 2013.

notes: SIZING SANITY CHECK: ENA records 27 Klebsiella samples (ena_taxon_samples=27, ena_total_samples=27) for this accession, yet the associated paper describes 227 Salmonella genomes deposited under PRJEB32657. The paper has zero coverage of Klebsiella. The 27 Klebsiella samples are likely incidental co-isolates or contaminants detected during an E. coli / Salmonella household surveillance study; they are not described anywhere in the paper. study_setting.evidence_quote: clinical isolates from Ghana (EBI study description); A total of 36 non-redundant Acinetobacter clinical isolates were recovered from different patients at three hospitals in Ghana

amr_study.evidence_quote: Our aim of the project is to investigate the current status of antimicrobial resistance among clinical isolates from Ghana, and further to explore major resistance mechanisms involved.

coverage_basis: The provided paper (Frontiers in Microbiology 2020) is entirely about Acinetobacter spp. from Ghana; 36 clinical Acinetobacter isolates are described and 4 complete genomes deposited under PRJNA473419. No Klebsiella records are mentioned anywhere in the text. ENA shows 25 Klebsiella samples under this umbrella BioProject. Paper coverage for Klebsiella = 0/25 = 0%. Study-level attributes are graded solely from the EBI study description, which applies to the whole project.

country.evidence_quote: clinical isolates from Ghana (EBI study description); isolates were recovered from different patients at three hospitals in Ghana (Tamale Teaching Hospital, Cape Coast Teaching Hospital, and Effia Nkwanta Regional Hospital)

host.evidence_quote: clinical isolates from Ghana (EBI study description); isolates recovered from different patients

notes: TAXON MISMATCH: The provided paper is entirely about Acinetobacter spp.; it contains zero Klebsiella records. The ENA shows 25 Klebsiella samples (= all 25 total samples) under umbrella BioProject PRJNA473419 ('Ghana AMR research project organized by TMDU and NMIMR'). Paper coverage for Klebsiella = 0%. A separate, unidentified publication almost certainly describes the Klebsiella component of this TMDU/NMIMR Ghana collaboration but was not provided. amr_target and amr_method are not_gradeable because amr_study = surveillance (the EBI description states the sampling frame is 'clinical isolates', with AMR investigated afterward, not used as a pre-selection criterion). Collection dates from the Acinetobacter paper (2016–2017) were not backfilled to Klebsiella samples given 0% paper coverage. Country (Ghana) and host (human) are backed directly by the EBI study description and are applied whole-project.
